newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stark says Germany to meet EMU deficit goal in 97.
newsitem.headline: Stark says Germany to meet EMU deficit goal in 97.

text.p: A senior German finance ministry official repeated on Tuesday that Germany in 1997 would meet deficit criteria needed to qualify for membership in Europe's monetary union slated to begin in January 1999.

"I think that with the newest numbers that we have put together, the 2.9 percent budget deficit ratio (as compared with Gross Domestic Product) for 1997, we will fulfil the Maastricht Treaty deficit criteria," Juergen Stark, state secretary in the finance ministry, told journalists.
"And in this 2.9 percent, we have already considered all currently known risks, including a rise in the average increase in the unemployment level of around 200,000 (for all of 1997)," he said.

Stark said Bonn would have to await further budget developments, adding that January unemployment data was particularly high due to a number of special factors, such as the cold weather, that should decline in the coming months.
Asked when a budget freeze might be enacted by Bonn, Stark said, "I do not know."
Stark made similar comments to journalists on Monday after a meeting of European finance ministers in Brussels. --Svea Herbst-Bayliss, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
